extracted.intended_audience: general readers and students of theatre history / American literary biography
extracted.subtask_description: Expository/biographical chapter about the life, habits, values, and professional activities of 19th‑century American actor Edwin Forrest, with reflective commentary on training, morals, and efforts to foster a national drama.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-education and literary/cultural polish
rubrics_metrics.description: He became a liberal buyer of books, and soon had an excellent library... He read as a student, reflecting on what he read, striving to improve his mind and taste by knowledge in general, as well as to pierce more deeply into the philosophy of the dramatic art in particular. He made himself familiar with the history of plastic and pictorial art, with engravings of celebrated statues and paintings... He also explored the history of costume in the principal countries, classic, mediæval, and modern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Devote leisure to serious, reflective reading; read not idly but as a student, connecting general knowledge (biography, poetry, philosophy, science) to dramatic art; study related visual arts and costume history to inform theatrical practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain rigorous physical regimen
rubrics_metrics.description: While thus devoting himself with new zeal to mental culture, he did not forego one whit of his old assiduity in exercises for the furtherance of his bodily development... Forrest had pretty thoroughly practised gymnastics, the exercises of the military drill, horsemanship, and fencing... He took a series of lessons in boxing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular physical training (gymnastics, drill, horsemanship, fencing, boxing) is essential to build stamina, clean joints, and a reservoir of vitality that sustains performance and resists the exhausting demands of the profession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral code for practitioners of boxing (manly art)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hernizer...talked with him for half an hour in a wise and kindly manner on the morality of the art... He warned him especially never to lose his temper, and never to presume on the advantages of his skill to strike any man unnecessarily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approach combative training with restraint and ethical discipline: cultivate 'reserved power' so skill fosters generosity and forbearance rather than gratuitous violence; temper prevents misuse of strength.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artistic drill as distinctive discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The drill of the horseman, the sportsman, the boxer, the soldier, the dancer, the singer, the orator, has an effect quite distinct from and superior to that of labor or exercise. Labor or exercise is straggling, broken, fitful; but drill is regular, symmetric, rhythmical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursue 'artistic drill'—regular, symmetric, rhythmical practice—as opposed to fitful exercise; drill economizes and directs forces, refines and exalts technique, fosters self-respect, confidence, self-possession, and high-level mastery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of financial patronage to foster national drama (prize conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: To the author of the best Tragedy, in five acts, of which the hero or principal character shall be an aboriginal of this country, the sum of five hundred dollars, and half of the proceeds of the third representation, with my own gratuitous services on that occasion. The award to be made by a committee of literary and theatrical gentlemen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design incentives with clear formal conditions (genre, structure, required subject matter), specify monetary reward and theatre-related remuneration, and appoint a reputable adjudicating committee; such premiums can stimulate native dramatic production even if many submissions fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee adjudication and standards in prize selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee selected by Forrest consisted of his friends Bryant, Halleck, Lawson, Leggett, Wetmore, and Brooks... Fourteen plays were presented in competition, and the prize was adjudged to Metamora... In the last instance about eighty productions were forwarded to the judges, and, as not one of them was thought to meet the conditions assigned, Forrest sent his check for a thousand dollars to the author of Mohammed, as that was considered the most effective composition, though not well adapted to the stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a committee of respected literary/theatrical figures; be prepared to reject submissions that fail to meet conditions while still recognizing merit (e.g., a monetary award even if the play is not stage-suitable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial prudence, temperance, and filial duty
rubrics_metrics.description: He resolved to heed the lesson, to be industrious, temperate, and prudent, and to husband his earnings... collecting everything he possessed, he went from New York to Philadelphia, paid the debts his father had left... bought a house in the name of his mother and sisters, and deposited in the bank to their account all he had remaining, thus securing them a handsome support whatever might happen to him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine generosity with prudence: avoid reckless profusion, practice saving and responsible financial management, especially to secure family welfare; temperance helps avoid professional pitfalls like intemperance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of cultivated physical perfection for moral and artistic excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the strength, grace, discipline, smiling fearlessness, superb hardihood... that evoke admiration. Surely it is better to be a perfect animal than an imperfect one. When all things are in harmony, the finest corporeal condition is the basis for the highest spiritual power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate bodily form and discipline as a foundation for higher artistic and moral achievements; physical excellence confers confidence and presence beneficial to public performance.
